Religions.Name: The Faith of the Six Flames
Religions.Description: The Empire believes that the world is lit by six eternal flames, each representing a divine power. Together, they illuminate civilization and guide mortals through life, war, and death.  Temples often depict six braziers burning in unison, symbolizing harmony among the gods.
Religions.History: The Faith of the Six Flames began in the heart of the Empire, where Caldaros was exalted as the divine Emperor. Priests taught that six sacred flames embodied justice, mercy, war, wisdom, fertility, and death, each burning in eternal harmony. As the Empire expanded, the faith spread and adapted to local cultures, giving rise to three regional variations: South: Emphasized mercy and fertility, blending Imperial rites with agrarian traditions. North: Focused on war and endurance, appealing to frontier soldiers and settlers. West: Elevated wisdom and justice, aligning with noble courts and feudal governance.
Religions.Creation: In the beginning, the world was dark and cold. The Six Flames descended from the heavens, each lighting a part of existence — courage, wisdom, toil, mercy, war, and death. Together, they brought balance and order.
Religions.Life: Mortals are born from the sparks of Doros’ forge, given breath by Serona’s mercy, and guided by Aurethia’s wisdom. Calradios grants them courage to face trials, while Veyros teaches them the strength to defend their kin.
Religions.Death: When life ends, Mortranos extinguishes the mortal flame and carries the soul across the Twilight River. There, the soul is judged by Calradios for bravery and justice, and placed among the Six Flames according to the virtues it upheld.
Religions.Cycle: Souls that lived with balance are reborn into the world, their spark reignited by Doros. Those who falter are given penance in the shadow of Mortranos until they are ready to return.

Dieties.Name: Calradios, the Dragon Emperor
Dieties.Title: The Flame of Valor
Dieties.Description: Once a mortal emperor who united the land, Calradios ascended into godhood. Depicted as a dragon-crowned warrior, he embodies courage, honor, and the defense of law. His worship is strongest in the Empire’s heartlands.

Dieties.Name: Aurethia
Dieties.Title: The Flame of Wisdom
Dieties.Description: Goddess of scrolls, stars, and hidden truths. Scholars and magistrates pray to her for clarity in judgment and mastery of learning. Her temples double as libraries.

Dieties.Name: Mortranos
Dieties.Title: The Flame of Twilight
Dieties.Description: A hooded figure who guides souls to the afterlife. He is not feared but respected, for he ensures balance between the living and the dead. Priests of Mortranos oversee funerary rites.

Dieties.Name: Veyros
Dieties.Title: The Flame of Iron
Dieties.Description: Patron of soldiers and generals. His flame burns in every legion camp. He is depicted with a sword in one hand and a broken shield in the other, symbolizing both conquest and sacrifice

Dieties.Name: Serona
Dieties.Title: The Flame of Mercy
Dieties.Description: Gentle goddess of compassion, healing, and charity. She is invoked by healers, midwives, and those who care for the poor. Her flame is said to soothe even the fiercest warrior’s heart

Dieties.Name: Doros
Dieties.Title: The Flame of Toil
Dieties.Description: God of farmers, builders, and craftsmen. Doros is depicted with calloused hands and a hammer. His worship emphasizes diligence, humility, and the sanctity of honest work.

Traits.Name: Women in Rituals
Traits.Description: Women can serve as Flamebearers (high priests), and female warriors are celebrated as embodiments of Calradios’ bravery tempered by Serona’s mercy.
Traits.Bonus: No social stigma for female leaders.

Sects.Cycle: Souls that lived with balance are reborn into the world, their spark reignited by Doros. Those who falter are given penance in the shadow of Mortranos until they are ready to return.  Calradios entrusted Serona with the “keys of rebirth,” making her the gatekeeper of reincarnation. This gives women symbolic power over the cycle of life.
Sects.Description: The Empire believes that the world is lit by six eternal flames, each representing a divine power. Together, they illuminate civilization and guide mortals through life, war, and death.  Temples often depict six braziers burning in unison, symbolizing harmony among the gods. Calradios entrusted Serona with the “keys of rebirth,” making her the gatekeeper of reincarnation. This gives women symbolic power over the cycle of life.

Traits.Name: Elevation of Doros
Traits.Description: Doros is revered as the Enduring Flame. Farmers, builders, and miners are considered the backbone of society, and festivals honor toil and survival.
Traits.Bonus: No negative social bonus to female leaders.

Sects.Death: When life ends, Mortranos extinguishes the mortal flame and carries the soul across the Twilight River. There, the soul is judged by Calradios for bravery and justice, and placed among the Six Flames according to the virtues it upheld. Mortranos is worshiped with harsher rituals — bodies are burned in great pyres to “release the flame quickly” in the cold north
Sects.Description: The Empire believes that the world is lit by six eternal flames, each representing a divine power. Together, they illuminate civilization and guide mortals through life, war, and death.  Calradios’ dragon breath forged the northern mountains, and Doros hammered them into shape. Hardship is seen as divine testing.

Traits.Name: Elevation of Veyros
Traits.Description: Veyros is the Dominant Flame. Military service is considered sacred, and temples often double as training grounds
Traits.Bonus: No negative social bonus to female leaders.

Sects.Description: The Empire believes that the world is lit by six eternal flames, each representing a divine power. Together, they illuminate civilization and guide mortals through life, war, and death.  Calradios is depicted more as a conqueror than a just ruler. Justice is interpreted as victory in battle. They believe souls judged worthy by Calradios join Veyros’ eternal legion, fighting in the heavens until reborn.

Religions.Name: The Faith of the Five Torches
Religions.Description: When the Vlandians came into contact with the Empire, their paganism was gradually replaced by the Faith of the Flames. The process was not immediate — it was political, cultural, and military.  As the Empire expanded westward, Vlandian nobles sought legitimacy by adopting the Empire’s religion. Temples were built in place of groves, and priests of the Six Flames were installed in towns.  Vlandians reject Calradios as a false god-emperor — they see him as an imperial replacement for their Sky-Father. They call their gods Torches, each representing a guiding light for mortal life. Temples are built like stone keeps, with five blazing torches lit at all times. Stronger emphasis on knightly honor, peasant toil, and the equality of death.
Religions.History: The Faith of the Five Torches emerged in Vlandia during the uneasy transition from paganism to Imperial religion. Originally, Vlandians worshipped gods of sky, earth, wolves, rivers, and ancestors. When Imperial missionaries arrived, these deities were reinterpreted as torches — lesser lights beneath the Six Flames. The turning point came under King Alaric of Vlandia, who formally adopted the Faith to secure Imperial recognition and legitimacy. Pagan rites were outlawed, but folk traditions survived in secret, fueling later sectarian tensions between Imperial orthodoxy and rural clans.
Religions.Creation: The Five Torches were lit by the First King, a mortal chosen by the gods to bring order to chaos.
Religions.Life: Aldric grants wisdom, Serenya grants mercy, Durand grants strength of hand, and Veymar grants courage. Together they sustain mortal life.
Religions.Death: Morthain extinguishes the mortal torch and guides souls into the Hall of Ashes, where they await rebirth.
Religions.Cycle: Souls who lived with balance are rekindled by Durand’s forge and return to the world. Those who sought tyranny (like Calradios) are cast into eternal shadow.

Dieties.Name: Aldric
Dieties.Title: The Torch of Lore
Dieties.Description: Patron of scribes and judges. His name comes from old Vlandian meaning “wise ruler.” His priests keep chronicles and advise lords.

Dieties.Name: Morthain
Dieties.Title: The Torch of Shadows
Dieties.Description: A grim reaper figure, cloaked and skeletal. He is impartial, guiding souls to the afterlife. His cult is strong among peasants who see him as the great equalizer

Dieties.Name: Veymar
Dieties.Title: The Torch of Steel
Dieties.Description: Patron of knights and mercenaries. Depicted with a greatsword and battered helm. His worship emphasizes martial honor and defense of one’s liege.

Dieties.Name: Serenya
Dieties.Title: The Torch of Grace
Dieties.Description: A maternal figure, invoked by healers and midwives. Her mercy is seen as noble charity, binding lords to care for their vassals.

Dieties.Name: Durand
Dieties.Title: The Torch of Toil
Dieties.Description: Patron of farmers, masons, and craftsmen. His name echoes “endurance.” He is depicted with a hammer and plow, symbolizing the dignity of work.

Religions.Name: Vlandian Paganism
Religions.Description: The Vlandians, before adopting the Empire’s religion, had a tribal, warrior-centered faith rooted in nature and ancestor worship.

Dieties.Name: The Sky-Father (Weyric)
Dieties.Title: Lord of Oaths
Dieties.Description: God of thunder, sky, and authority. Lords swore fealty beneath his storms, believing his lightning sealed their vows.

Dieties.Name: Thyra, the Earth-Mother
Dieties.Title: Keeper of the Hearth
Dieties.Description: Goddess of soil, crops, and family. Farmers prayed to her for abundance, and women invoked her during childbirth.

Dieties.Name: Fenric, the Wolf-Spirit
Dieties.Title: Guardian of the Pack
Dieties.Description: Patron of warriors and raiders. Wolves were sacred animals, symbolizing ferocity in battle and loyalty to kin.

Dieties.Name: The River-Sisters
Dieties.Title: Maidens of the Stream
Dieties.Description: Minor spirits tied to rivers, wells, and springs. Travelers sought their protection, and seers claimed visions from their waters.

Dieties.Name: Ancestor Shades
Dieties.Title: Voices of the Mounds
Dieties.Description: Spirits of dead chieftains, honored in burial mounds. Believed to guide descendants in war and counsel leaders through dreams.

Religions.Name: Whispering Wilds
Religions.Description: The Whispering Wilds is less a structured religion and more a living dialogue with nature. It emphasizes harmony with the forest, respect for ancestors, and channeling animal spirits in war. Unlike the Empire’s centralized temples, Battanian worship is performed in sacred groves, stone circles, and riverbanks.
Religions.History: The Whispering Wilds has long been the lifeblood of the Battanian clans, a faith rooted in shamanism and animism that sees spirits in every tree, river, and beast. For centuries it bound the people together through sacred groves, ancestor feasts, and the guidance of shamans who spoke with the voices of the wild.  Yet in recent generations, the faith has come under strain. Immigration from neighboring peoples has brought new customs and beliefs into Battanian lands, diluting the old traditions. Imperial holy men, spreading the word of the Six Flames, have found converts among ambitious nobles and merchants eager for legitimacy and trade. Most perilous of all, the Battanians’ steady loss of territory — and the bitter defeats that accompany it — have shaken confidence in the spirits’ protection.  Though the Whispering Wilds remains the primary religion of the Battanian peoples, its voice grows weaker. Shamans still lead rituals in forest circles, and peasants cling to charms and omens, but each lost battle and each new convert to the Flames chips away at its strength. The faith now stands at a crossroads: either it adapts to survive, or it risks fading into memory, a whisper drowned out by the march of foreign gods.
Religions.Creation: In the beginning, the world was a silent forest. The First Shaman lit a fire, and from its smoke rose the spirits — stag, raven, wolf, and oak — who gave voice to the land.
Religions.Life: Mortals are born from the soil of the Earth-Mother, given breath by the winds of the Sky-Father, and guided by animal spirits that choose them at birth.
Religions.Death: When a mortal dies, their spirit is carried by the Raven into the Shadowed Glade, where ancestors dwell. There, they feast and counsel the living through dreams.
Religions.Cycle: Souls may return to the world, reborn as new warriors or hunters, or remain among the ancestors to guard the clan. The cycle depends on whether the spirit’s duty is fulfilled.

Dieties.Name: Cernach, the Stag-Lord
Dieties.Title: Horned Guardian
Dieties.Description: Patron of chieftains and hunters. His antlers symbolize authority and the bounty of the forest.

Dieties.Name: Branna, the Raven
Dieties.Title: The Flame of Wisdom
Dieties.Description: Guide of souls to the Shadowed Glade. Ravens are seen as omens of death and prophecy.

Dieties.Name: Fenra, the Wolf-Mother
Dieties.Title: Keeper of the Pack
Dieties.Description: Spirit of warriors and clans. Wolves embody ferocity in battle and devotion to kin.

Dieties.Name: Thalos, the Sky-Father
Dieties.Title: Voice of Thunder
Dieties.Description: God of the sky, storms, and sacred oaths. His lightning punishes oath-breakers.

Dieties.Name: Eira, the Earth-Mother
Dieties.Title: Root of Life
Dieties.Description: Goddess of soil, crops, and family. She sustains mortals with her endless bounty.

Dieties.Name: Sylwen, the River-Maiden
Dieties.Title: Mist of Dreams
Dieties.Description: Spirit of rivers and wells. Shamans seek visions in her waters.

Dieties.Name: Druan, the Oak-Spirit
Dieties.Title: Ancient Sentinel
Dieties.Description: Embodiment of the sacred groves. Oaks are seen as eternal witnesses of history.

Dieties.Name: Cael, the Fire-Sprite
Dieties.Title: Flame of Renewal
Dieties.Description: Minor spirit of fire, invoked in rituals and feasts. Fire is seen as a bridge between worlds.

Dieties.Name: Ancestor Shades
Dieties.Title: Voices of the Glade
Dieties.Description: Spirits of fallen heroes and chieftains. They advise descendants through dreams and omens.

Religions.Name: Faith of the Three Faces
Religions.Description: The Nords believe their god is one being with three faces, each governing a vital element of survival in the harsh north. To appease the god, sacrifices are made to each face in its own way. The fallen face, however, is seen as the source of chaos, storms, and destruction — a reminder of the cost of freedom.  Captives are bound to the Land Face until their debt is repaid. Slavery is temporary, closer to indentured servitude, with more freedom than peasants.
Religions.History: The Faith of the Three Faces is the harsh monotheism of the Nords, worshipping a single god with three aspects: Land, Wind, and Water. Each face demands sacrifice — blood spilled on foreign soil, hanging, or drowning — to sustain the balance of the world. Yet the god is fractured: a fallen face betrayed the unity by granting mortals freedom of choice, and now rules a frozen hell of blizzards and storms. Warriors who die in battle are carried to the Hall of Eternal Glory, while cowards are condemned to the fallen face’s torment. This faith reflects the Nord ethos: raiding as necessity, slavery as survival, and honor as the only path to eternity.
Religions.Creation: The god of Three Faces shaped the land, stirred the winds, and filled the seas. Together, these aspects gave mortals life and order. But one face fell, granting humans freedom of choice, betraying the unity of the god.
Religions.Life: Mortals live under the balance of the three faces. They must appease each through sacrifice: hanging for wind, drowning for water, and blood spilled on foreign soil for land. Women, as keepers of the hearth and household, are seen as guardians of continuity while men raid abroad.
Religions.Death: Warriors who die in battle are carried into the Hall of Eternal Glory, where they feast, fight, and drink forever. Those who die craven or surrender are dragged into the frozen hell of the fallen face, tormented by blizzards and storms.
Religions.Cycle: Honor sustains the cycle. Brave souls remain in the Hall of Eternal Glory; dishonored souls are trapped in the frozen wastes. There is no rebirth — only eternal reward or punishment.

Dieties.Name: The Land Face
Dieties.Title: Stone of Strength
Dieties.Description: Embodies the earth, stability, and conquest. Appeased by blood spilled on foreign soil.

Dieties.Name: The Wind Face
Dieties.Title: Voice of Oaths
Dieties.Description: Governs storms, oaths, and freedom of spirit. Appeased by sacrifice through hanging.

Dieties.Name: The Water Face
Dieties.Title: Depth of Fate
Dieties.Description: Rules rivers, seas, and journeys. Appeased by sacrifice through drowning.  Women manage households, farms, and trade while men raid. They are respected as spiritual keepers of continuity, tied to the Water Face’s life-giving role.

Dieties.Name: The Fallen Face
Dieties.Title: Breaker of Unity
Dieties.Description: Once part of the god, but betrayed the core three by giving mortals freedom of choice. Now rules the frozen hell, sending blizzards, tsunamis, and earthquakes to hinder Nord raids.

Sects.Description: The outlawed practice could be remembered in myth — perhaps the weather deity whispers to remote clans to keep the old ways alive, linking cannibalism to corruption.

Religions.Name: The Hearth of Six
Religions.Description: The Sturgians believe in six sacred hearths, each representing a divine principle.  Five hearths are singular deities tied to survival and community.  The Sixth Hearth is unique: a multi-faced deity embodying Land, Wind, and Water — the primal forces of the north.  Caldaros, unlike in Nord belief, is accepted as part of this sixth hearth, seen as the Emperor who brought order and legitimacy.
Religions.History: The Sturgians, like their Nord cousins, originally practiced animistic faiths tied to forests, rivers, and ancestral spirits. Hearth fires were already central to their survival in the frozen north, symbolizing family and continuity. As Sturgian clans migrated southward and began trading with Imperial merchants, they encountered the Faith of the Six Flames. Imperial priests emphasized fire as divine order, which resonated with the Sturgians’ own hearth-centered worldview. Sturgian chieftains saw adopting the Empire’s religion as a way to gain recognition and legitimacy in dealings with Imperial lords. By honoring Caldaros as divine, they aligned themselves with Imperial authority while still retaining their independence. Instead of worshipping “flames,” the Sturgians reinterpreted them as hearths — warmer, more communal symbols suited to their climate. The sixth hearth became the supreme one, embodying the primal forces of land, wind, and water, with Caldaros added as its fourth face.
Religions.Creation: The First Clan lit six hearths to survive the endless winter. From each flame rose a spirit. The sixth hearth burned brightest, revealing itself as a god with three faces — Land, Wind, and Water — later joined by Caldaros as its fourth face.
Religions.Life: Mortals live by the hearths. Each hearth sustains a different part of life: food, family, trade, war, wisdom. The sixth hearth governs the natural forces and kingship.
Religions.Death: Souls who honor the hearths are welcomed into the Hall of the Hearthfire, a communal afterlife of warmth and feasting. Those who betray oaths or abandon kin are cast into the cold wastes.
Religions.Cycle: Souls may return through the hearth’s flame, reborn into new generations, or remain with ancestors as guardians of the clan.

Dieties.Name: Hrodan’s Hearth
Dieties.Title: Keeper of Kin
Dieties.Description: Embodies the warmth of family bonds and household survival.

Dieties.Name: Brynja’s Hearth
Dieties.Title: Mother of Plenty
Dieties.Description: Goddess of crops, livestock, and the hearth’s daily fire.

Dieties.Name: Eirik’s Hearth
Dieties.Title: Blade of the Hearth
Dieties.Description: Patron of warriors, raids, and defense of clan lands.

Dieties.Name: Torvald’s Hearth
Dieties.Title: Voice of Counsel
Dieties.Description: Spirit of law, wisdom, and fair trade among clans.

Dieties.Name: Skara’s Hearth
Dieties.Title: Watcher of Ashes
Dieties.Description: Guardian of ancestral spirits, honored in burial mounds.

Dieties.Name: The Great Hearth
Dieties.Title: Flame of the World
Dieties.Description: The supreme deity with three primal faces (soil, sky, sea) and a fourth face revealed as Caldaros, the Emperor.

Religions.Name: The Path of Sun and Moon
Religions.Description: The Path of Sun and Moon teaches that life is a balance between extremes: the burning trial of the Sun and the gentle guidance of the Moon. The Aserai believe survival in the desert requires discipline, hygiene, and self-reliance. Kings and clan leaders are respected not because they are divinely chosen, but because they have proven themselves worthy in the eyes of their people — their success is seen as the Sun’s blessing upon their merit.
Religions.History: - Long before kings and clans, the desert tribes wandered without unity. Asera, a wise patriarch, was said to have stood beneath the blazing Sun and the guiding Moon, declaring that survival in the desert required balance between discipline and mercy. He taught that the Sun (Shams) demanded cleanliness, strength, and toil, while the Moon (Qamar) offered guidance, dreams, and respite.Asera lit the First Fire of Purity, a ritual hearth where tribes washed themselves and swore oaths of discipline. He then raised the Silver Banner of the Moon, calling his people to follow the stars and live as individuals judged by their own merit. Through these acts, he bound the duality of Sun and Moon into a single path.His descendants and followers became known as Banu Asera — “Children of Asera.” They carried his teachings across the desert, uniting scattered clans into a culture defined by hygiene, meritocracy, and balance. To this day, every Aserai clan traces its legitimacy back to Asera’s wisdom, not divine appointment.Kings and clan leaders are respected because they prove themselves worthy, echoing Asera’s belief that leadership is earned, not inherited. The Sun blesses their strength, the Moon blesses their wisdom, but it is their own merit that raises them above others.This makes Asera the cultural anchor: a patriarch who interpreted the Sun and Moon, founded the rituals of hygiene and meritocracy, and gave the people their name.

Lore.Name: The Tale of Asera’s Vision
Lore.Passage: Long ago, when the tribes wandered without unity, Asera walked alone into the desert. The sands burned beneath his feet, and the sky was a furnace. He collapsed, parched and weary, and raised his eyes to the blazing Sun.The Sun spoke: “Rise, Asera. My fire will test you. Keep yourself pure, keep yourself strong, and you will endure.” With trembling hands, Asera washed the dust from his skin with the last of his water, and he felt the Sun’s blessing in his discipline.That night, as he lay beneath the stars, the Moon rose full and silver. The Moon whispered: “Rest, Asera. My light will guide you. Seek wisdom, seek balance, and you will lead.” Asera followed the Moon’s path across the sky, and in his dreams he saw the tribes gathered around a single fire, united. When dawn came, Asera lit a great hearth from the embers of his vision. He taught the people: “The Sun demands purity and strength. The Moon grants mercy and guidance. Together they are the path. Follow it, and we will endure.” From that day, the tribes called themselves Banu Asera, the Children of Asera, for he had shown them the way of Sun and Moon.

Lore.Name: Sunrise Prayer
Lore.Passage: Burning Lord, keeper of strength, I rise with your fire. Cleanse me with light, Harden me with trial, Bless my labor, That I may endure as Banu Asera.

Lore.Name: Moonrise Prayer
Lore.Passage: Gentle Lady, watcher of dreams, I walk beneath your silver path. Guide me with mercy, Balance me with wisdom, Bless my rest,That I may endure as Banu Asera.

Religions.Creation: From the first dawn, the Sun and Moon rose as twins. The Sun gave heat, light, and trial; the Moon gave coolness, guidance, and rest. Together they shaped the desert and its people.
Religions.Life: Mortals live between the cycles of Sun and Moon. The Sun demands discipline, hygiene, and strength; the Moon offers mercy, wisdom, and dreams.
Religions.Death: Souls are judged by balance. Those who lived with honor and discipline are welcomed into the Garden of Twilight, where Sun and Moon meet in harmony. Those who lived in excess or corruption wander the endless desert storms.
Religions.Cycle: The Sun and Moon endlessly chase each other across the sky, symbolizing the eternal rhythm of struggle and renewal.

Dieties.Name: Shams (The Sun)
Dieties.Title: The Burning Lord
Dieties.Description: Embodies strength, hygiene, and trial. Blesses those who prove themselves through talent and discipline.

Dieties.Name: Qamar (The Moon)
Dieties.Title: The Gentle Lady
Dieties.Description: Embodies wisdom, respite, and balance. Guides travelers by night and judges souls with compassion.

Sects.Life: Followers believe Asera was chosen by Shams and Qamar to embody balance. Life is lived by following his teachings of discipline, hygiene, and merit.
Sects.Death: Those who honor Asera are welcomed into his eternal hearth, where he sits beside the Sun and Moon. Those who reject him are cast into the desert storms.

Dieties.Name: Asera
Dieties.Title: The Star
Dieties.Description: Revered not just as patriarch but as demi-god, the living incarnation of balance between Sun and Moon.

Religions.Name: Sāni al-Shumū
Religions.Description: In the southernmost towns of the Aserai lands, migrants brought with them the worship of the Candlemaker, known locally as Ṣāniʿ al-Shumūʿ. This god is said to light a candle at each birth and snuff it at each death, symbolizing the fragility of life. The faith has spread quickly among the poor, who see their struggles reflected in the flickering flame. Its message of predestination undermines the Aserai meritocracy, whispering that destiny is fixed rather than earned, and so it grows as a quiet challenge to the Path of Sun and Moon.
Religions.Life: Each person’s life is a candle lit by the Candlemaker. The flame represents vitality, and its strength depends on the purity of one’s actions. Followers emphasize humility, endurance, and acceptance of fate.
Religions.Death: At death, the Candlemaker snuffs out the flame. The soul is said to vanish into darkness, with no afterlife promised — only the memory of the candle’s light remains.
Religions.Cycle: Life is predetermined; the Candlemaker alone decides when a flame is lit and when it is extinguished. There is no rebirth, only the inevitability of the snuffing.

Dieties.Name: Sāni al-Shumū
Dieties.Title: The Candlemaker
Dieties.Description: a solitary god who holds all lives in his hands, lighting and extinguishing candles as he wills.

Religions.Name: Followers of Marg-Saheb
Religions.Description: From the southeast came a grim faith devoted to a god of death and destruction. Its followers believe the world is ending, and only through grisly sacrifice can they stave off annihilation. Enemies are skinned alive, their hides displayed as offerings to the Flayed God, whose hunger is said to be endless. Though not widely practiced, the cult’s violence has made it infamous. Raids, terror, and forced sacrifices destabilize borderlands, leaving the Aserai wary of its spread and fearful of its zealotry.
Religions.History: The cult of Marg-Saheb, the Lord of Death, is a grim faith that spread into the Aserai lands from the southeast. Its followers believe the world is nearing its end, and only through blood and skin-offerings can they appease their god before the final destruction. Unlike the Candlemaker’s quiet spread among the poor or the reverent but harmless worship of Asera, the Followers of Marg-Saheb destabilize trade, sow fear, and fracture clan unity. To many, they are not merely heretics but harbingers of ruin, a shadow looming over the Path of Sun and Moon.
Religions.Life: Life is seen as fleeting and meaningless, a temporary skin covering bone. Followers believe existence is only preparation for sacrifice
Religions.Death: Death is demanded by Marg-Saheb. Those flayed and offered to him are said to join his army of shadows, while those who die unoffered are devoured by his hunger.
Religions.Cycle: The cult teaches that the world is ending. Each sacrifice delays the apocalypse by a single day, but the cycle of destruction cannot be stopped.

Dieties.Name: Marg-Saheb
Dieties.Title: Lord of Death
Dieties.Description: a god of decay and annihilation, who strips flesh from mortals and consumes the world piece by piece.
